Brotherhood
BRUHþH-er-hood
n.
Brother + -hood (state, condition). Renders the Greek adelphotēs, “the brotherhood,” from adelphos (brother)—the body of those who are brothers in Christ.

See also: Brotherhood

📖 Biblical Definition

Brotherhood is Peter’s name for the body of believers considered as the new family God has constituted in Christ—all who share by faith in the same Father, the same elder Brother (Christ Himself), the same indwelling Spirit, and the same inheritance: fear God. Honour the king. Love the brotherhood (1 Pet 2:17); knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world (1 Pet 5:9). The category is structural for New Testament Christianity. Christ Himself, by His incarnation, has made the saints His brothers: both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren (Heb 2:11-12). Believers are repeatedly addressed as brethren across the epistles (over 230 times); they call one another brother and sister; they consider one another members of the same family of God. The brotherhood has therefore specific duties. It is to be loved: love the brotherhood is a standing apostolic command (1 Pet 2:17), let brotherly love continue is the standing apostolic discipline (Heb 13:1), and Christ Himself names love of the brethren as the credential of His disciples (John 13:35). It is to be recognized: across natural borders, every brother in Christ is a brother regardless of his earthly nationality, social class, age, sex, or temperament. It is to be cared for: let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith (Gal 6:10); the saints have prior claim on the saints’ mercy without ever cutting off mercy to those outside. And it is to be defended: when one brother suffers, the brotherhood suffers; when one brother is persecuted, the brotherhood prays; when one brother sins, the brotherhood addresses him in Matt 18 process. The brotherhood is also to be visibly distinguishable from the world: by its love (John 13:35), by its unity (John 17:21), by its endurance of common afflictions (1 Pet 5:9), by its mutual care (Acts 2:42-47), and by its ordered life under Christ’s Headship and the apostolic Word. The brotherhood is no metaphor or fond sentiment; it is the actual constituted family of God in Christ, with real members, real ties, and real claims upon the members’ affections, time, money, and lives.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines BROTHERHOOD as the state or quality of being a brother; an association of men for any purpose; in scripture, the body of believers considered as the new family God has constituted in Christ.

expand to see more

BROTHERHOOD, n. — 1. The state or quality of being a brother; fraternity. 2. An association of men for any purpose, as a society of monks; a fraternity. 3. A class of men of the same kind, profession, or occupation. 4. In scripture, the body of believers as the family of God in Christ. Love the brotherhood (1 Pet 2:17).

📖 Key Scripture

1 Peter 2:17 — "Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king."

1 Peter 5:9 — "Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world."

Hebrews 2:11-12 — "For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee."

John 13:35 — "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Brotherhood is corrupted by the loose-affiliation register of contemporary church life that treats fellow-believers as fellow-attendees rather than as actual brothers and sisters with whom one shares the costly ties of a real family—and by the inverse corruption of the cultic in-group that treats brotherhood with such exclusive intensity that it severs healthy ties with family and society outside.

expand to see more

The loose-affiliation register has hollowed the New Testament category of brotherhood. The contemporary believer often relates to fellow-Christians as fellow-attendees of a Sunday service rather than as actual brothers and sisters in a real family. The ties are thin, the obligations are minimal, the love is real but bounded by the limits of weekly conversation. The New Testament’s brotherhood is sharper. The saints sold their possessions to supply the needs of fellow-saints (Acts 2:44-45; 4:34); they bore one another’s burdens (Gal 6:2); they suffered together when one member suffered (1 Cor 12:26); they exchanged real hospitality, real care, real letters of recommendation, real material support across the long miles. Recover the doctrine, and the saint recovers also the practices: actual time spent with actual brothers and sisters in costly, sustained, embodied love, the kind that bears burdens and supplies needs and goes the distance.

The opposite corruption is the cultic in-group that treats brotherhood with such exclusive intensity that it severs healthy ties with family and society outside, isolates the believer from the broader common life, and absolutizes the in-group’s claims to the displacement of legitimate other claims (the natural family, civil society, neighbor-love beyond the in-group). The biblical brotherhood does not require this. Love the brotherhood stands together with honour all men (1 Pet 2:17); do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith (Gal 6:10) keeps the priority without abolishing the wider love. Recover both ends. Refuse the loose-affiliation that hollows the category, and refuse the cultic intensity that severs the saint from his other proper loves. The biblical brotherhood is real, costly, and visible to the world—and it is held together with honor of all men, love of neighbor, and faithfulness in every other sphere of God’s appointed obligations.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek adelphotēs (brotherhood, the body of brethren) from adelphos (brother)—the new family God has constituted in Christ, with real members, real ties, and real claims upon affection, time, money, and life.

expand to see more

Greek adelphotēs (G81) — the brotherhood, the body of brethren (1 Pet 2:17; 5:9).

Greek adelphos (G80) — brother (the great NT family vocabulary).

Greek philadelphia (G5360) — brotherly love (the affection proper to the brotherhood).

Hebrew ’āch (H251) — brother (the OT cousin term).

Usage

"Love the brotherhood—Peter’s standing apostolic command names the discipline of love proper to the new family in Christ."

"Christ is not ashamed to call the saints His brethren (Heb 2:11-12); the brotherhood is constituted by His incarnation and atoning work."

"Loose-affiliation hollows the category; cultic intensity severs healthy ties; biblical brotherhood is real, costly, and held together with honor of all men and love of neighbor."
